# Validator fixtures

Test data for `tests/test_validate.py`. Two vaults, whose content is fictional and carries no evidential weight.

- `minimal/` — one complete valid pass from source to chapter: one source per source type (document, publication, data), one distillate each, one assertion grounded across all three and declaring one phenomenon, one output paragraph with a grounded footnote and a posit. Its `knowledge/state.md` carries the source inventory `tools/inventory.py` generates from that file state, and its topic map and glossary entry carry the navigation regions the same tool generates. `python tools/validate.py tests/fixtures/minimal` passes clean and without a warning, computations included, and `python tools/inventory.py tests/fixtures/minimal --check` exits 0.
- `broken/` — one specimen per defect class the validator must catch: dead block reference, dead frontmatter target, topic outside the controlled topic set, orphan assertion, one-sided contested relation, illegal frontmatter, frontmatter that parses as a list rather than a map, a list-valued field carrying a bare string, source metadata without its declared fields, status without recorded checks, status above the anchors it rests on, core statement without a statement ID, core statement with two source anchors, missing computation script, a computation carrying an argument, a computation script outside `tools/analysis/`, unrecorded quotation check, footnote without keyword, footnote defined twice, marker without definition, mirror out of sync, grounding that skips or sidesteps its layer, empty grounding, duplicate block ID, duplicate statement ID, several distillates on one representation, a `phenomena` value naming a document outside the glossary, a `related` value naming a document that does not exist, a missing generated region, a stale generated region, and the six defects reported as warnings, an unfilled template placeholder, a document whose last check predates its own revision, a chapter paragraph carrying no footnote marker, a chapter taking one side of a contested pair, two assertions resting on the same grounding anchors, a footnote alias that renames the assertion it cites, and a file name outside the slug rule. Each fixture names its own defect in its lead sentence.

  Several distillates of `broken/` hang on `10_markdown/documents/note`, which is a defect of its own (`E-SOURCE`) and at the same time what lets every other specimen rest on anchors that exist. The naming specimen is a glossary entry, because there the file name is the only thing under test, and its example region is current so that the name stays the only finding. `MOC-Broken.md` carries no markers at all, which is the missing-region specimen and keeps the orphan assertion out of a generated list at the same time.

The suite runs the validator over both and asserts that `minimal/` produces nothing and that every defect class in `broken/` is caught, which is what establishes that the validator catches anything at all. A further test parses the finding codes out of `tools/validate.py` and holds them against the specimen registries in `tests/test_validate.py`, so a check that gains no specimen and a specimen whose check disappeared both fail the suite. Deleting the fixtures leaves those tests running against directories that do not exist, where passing means nothing.

The validator reads only the content folders at the root it is given, so the fixtures stay invisible to a run over the vault itself and can be broken deliberately without touching the evidence layer.
